name: Portugal

train.sum: Santa Apolonia and Oriente are the main stations. CP runs Alfa Pendular and Intercity trains to Porto, and suburban lines to Sintra and Cascais.
train.sched: Suburban lines to Cascais and Sintra run frequently from early morning until late evening.
tickets: Lisbon to Sintra or Cascais: zone-based fare of a few euros one way
Lisbon to Porto: Alfa Pendular or Intercity, cheaper when booked early
Navegante card needed for suburban trains in the Lisbon area
train.tip: Cascais line departs from Cais do Sodre, Sintra line from Rossio.
buy: CP ticket offices and ticket machines in stations
CP website and CP app for Alfa Pendular and Intercidades. Seat reservation is compulsory
Sintra and Cascais lines: load zapping credit or a ticket on a navegante card (0.50 EUR) at station machines. Fertagus has its own tickets and machines
On board: generally not allowed. Only if the boarding station has no ticket sales, and then cash only, no extra fee
Without a valid ticket you can be fined 120 to 350 EUR on suburban and short regional trains, and 250 to 700 EUR on longer trips
Contactless bank cards do not work on CP trains. Buy and validate before you board

destinations.note: Crosses the 25 de Abril bridge, a train every 20 min
About 9 trains a day. Check which station your train uses
Arrives at Coimbra-B, outside the centre
Trains through the day. Arrives at Porto Campanha
Intercidades take about 3 h 30 min. Other Algarve stops include Albufeira-Ferreiras, Portimao and Lagos. Check which trains run direct
A few trains a day via Coimbra and Porto
On Intercidades trains towards Coimbra and Porto. Time is from Lisboa Oriente
On Intercidades trains towards Coimbra and Porto. Time is from Lisboa Oriente
On Intercidades trains towards Coimbra and Porto. Time is from Lisboa Oriente

tram.sum: Tram 28 climbs the old districts and is famous, but very crowded. The metro has 4 lines.
tram.sched: Metro 06:30 to 01:00. Tram 28 runs from early morning to evening.
tickets: Carris tram ticket on board: about 3.30 EUR, bus about 2.30 EUR
24-hour Carris and Metro ticket: about 7.25 EUR
tram.tip: Take Tram 28 early in the morning to avoid queues, or choose tram 12 instead.
buy: On board from the driver: about 3.30 EUR in cash. Small change only
Tap a contactless bank card on the reader by the door, about 3.30 EUR
Cheaper with a navegante card and zapping credit. Buy the card at metro machines or Carris shops
Bank cards do not work on the long trams of line 15E. Use navegante or cash

bus.sum: Carris buses cover Lisbon and Carris Metropolitana buses cover the wider region. Rede Expressos runs coaches to other cities.
bus.sched: Day buses from early morning to about midnight, with some night routes.
tickets: Navegante Municipal monthly pass: about 30 EUR
bus.tip: Top up Zapping credit and tap in each time you board, or tap a contactless bank card on Carris buses and trams.
buy: Carris buses: on board from the driver, about 2.30 EUR in cash
Carris buses: tap a contactless bank card on the reader, about 2.30 EUR
Cheaper with a navegante card and zapping credit, from metro machines or Carris shops
Carris Metropolitana: use navegante. Only some routes take bank cards
Rede Expressos coaches: buy online

airport.sum: Humberto Delgado Airport (LIS) is close to the city centre.
airport.sched: Metro red line reaches the centre in about 20 minutes.
tickets: Metro: about 1.90 EUR plus 0.50 EUR for the navegante card
Taxi from the airport: fixed fares since October 2026, about 16 to 23 EUR by zone and time
Train from Oriente: connections to Porto
airport.tip: The metro is the cheapest way from LIS to the city. For a taxi, buy a voucher at the Turismo de Lisboa desk in arrivals or pay the driver.
buy: Metro red line: navegante card (0.50 EUR) plus a single at the machines or ticket office, or tap a contactless bank card at the gates
Carris bus 783: about 2.30 EUR from the driver, or cheaper with navegante
Night bus 208 to Oriente and Cais do Sodre: Carris fares
No train at the airport. Take the metro to Oriente for CP trains
The Aerobus shuttle no longer runs

metro.note: Four metro lines: blue, yellow, green and red. The red line serves the airport. A new circular line is planned for 2027.
lines: Marques de Pombal links Blue and Yellow
Saldanha links Yellow and Red, and Alameda links Green and Red

tips: Lisbon is very hilly. A short taxi or ride-hail can save a tiring climb.
One navegante card works on metro, trams, buses and trains.
A contactless bank card works at metro gates and on Carris buses and trams, but not on CP trains.
